questions.text: A parallel plate capacitor with plate separation 5 mm is charged by a battery. On introducing a mica sheet of 2 mm and maintaining the connections of the plates with the terminals of the battery, it is found that it draws 25% more charge from the battery. The dielectric constant of mica is ____.
questions.sol_text:
Initial capacitor:
d = 5 mm
C = (epsilon_0 * A) / d
Q_1 = CV

After introducing mica sheet:
The mica sheet of 2 mm is inserted, leaving 3 mm of air gap.
New configuration has mica (2 mm) and air (3 mm) in series.

For capacitors in series:
C_eq = (C_1 * C_2) / (C_1 + C_2)

Where:
C_1 = (epsilon_0 * A) / 3 (air gap of 3 mm)
C_2 = (K * epsilon_0 * A) / 2 (mica of 2 mm with dielectric constant K)

C_eq = [(epsilon_0 * A / 3) * (K * epsilon_0 * A / 2)] / [(epsilon_0 * A / 3) + (K * epsilon_0 * A / 2)]

C_eq = [(epsilon_0 * A)^2 * K / 6] / [epsilon_0 * A * (1/3 + K/2)]

C_eq = [(epsilon_0 * A) * K / 6] / [(2 + 3K) / 6]

C_eq = (K * epsilon_0 * A) / (2 + 3K)

New charge:
Q_2 = C_eq * V = 1.25 * CV

Therefore:
(K * epsilon_0 * A) / (2 + 3K) * V = 1.25 * (epsilon_0 * A / 5) * V

(K * epsilon_0 * A) / (2 + 3K) = 1.25 * (epsilon_0 * A / 5)

K / (2 + 3K) = 0.25

K = 0.25(2 + 3K)

K = 0.5 + 0.75K

0.25K = 0.5

K = 2

questions.text: Three parallel plate capacitors each with area A and separation d are filled with two dielectric (k₁ and k₂) in the following fashion. Which of the following is true? (k₁ > k₂)
questions.sol_text:
For C_A:
Circuit shows k₁C and k₁C in series on top, k₂C and k₂C in series on bottom, with parallel connection between top and bottom.
C_A = (k₁C)/2 + (k₁k₂C)/(k₁ + k₂) = k₁C[(k₁ + 2k₂)/(2(k₁ + k₂))]

For C_B:
Circuit shows k₂C and k₁k₂C in series on top, k₁C and k₁k₂C in series on bottom.
C_B = (k₂C)/2 + (k₁k₂C)/(k₁ + k₂) = k₂C[(k₁ + 2k₂)/(2(k₁ + k₂))]

For C_C:
Circuit shows k₁C and k₂C in parallel on top, k₁C and k₂C in parallel on bottom, with series connection between top and bottom.
C_C = (2k₁k₂C)/(k₁ + k₂)

Comparison:
Given k₁ > k₂, we have:
C_A = k₁C[(k₁ + 2k₂)/(2(k₁ + k₂))]
C_B = k₂C[(k₁ + 2k₂)/(2(k₁ + k₂))]
C_C = (2k₁k₂C)/(k₁ + k₂)

Since k₁ > k₂:
C_A > C_B

Comparing C_A and C_C:
C_A/C_C = [k₁(k₁ + 2k₂)]/[4k₁k₂] = (k₁ + 2k₂)/(4k₂)

For k₁ > k₂: C_A > C_C

Comparing C_C and C_B:
C_C/C_B = [2k₁k₂]/[k₂(k₁ + 2k₂)/2] = 4k₁/(k₁ + 2k₂)

Since k₁ > k₂: C_C > C_B

Therefore: C_A > C_C > C_B

questions.text: There are three co-centric conducting spherical shells A, B and C of radii a, b and c respectively. The potential of the spheres A, B and C respectively, are:
options: (1/4πε₀)((q₁ + q₂ + q₃)/a), (1/4πε₀)((q₁ + q₂ + q₃)/b), (1/4πε₀)((q₁ + q₂ + q₃)/c)
(1/4πε₀)((q₁ + q₂ + q₃)/a), (1/4πε₀)((q₁ + q₂ + q₃)/b + q₃/c), (1/4πε₀)(q₁/a + q₂/b + q₃/c)
(1/4πε₀)(q₁/a + q₂/b + q₃/c), (1/4πε₀)(q₁/b + q₂/b + q₃/c), (1/4πε₀)(q₁ + q₂ + q₃)/c)
(1/4πε₀)(q₁/a + q₂/b + q₃/c), (1/4πε₀)(q₁ + q₂ + q₃)/b), (1/4πε₀)(q₁ + q₂ + q₃)/c)
questions.sol_text:
For three concentric conducting spherical shells with charges q₁, q₂, and q₃ on shells A, B, and C respectively:

The potential at any point is the superposition of potentials due to all three shells.

For shell A (radius a):
- It experiences potential due to its own charge q₁ at distance a
- Plus potential due to charge q₂ on shell B at distance a (since a < b)
- Plus potential due to charge q₃ on shell C at distance a (since a < c)

V_A = Kq₁/a + Kq₂/a + Kq₃/a is INCORRECT because charges on outer shells create potential as if concentrated at their own radius when viewed from inside.

Correct approach:
V_A = (1/4πε₀)(q₁/a + q₂/b + q₃/c)

For shell B (radius b):
- Potential due to q₁ at distance b: Kq₁/b
- Potential due to q₂ at distance b: Kq₂/b
- Potential due to q₃ at distance b: Kq₃/c (outer shell)

But since B is at radius b and q₂ is on B:
V_B = (1/4πε₀)(q₁/b + q₂/b + q₃/c)

For shell C (radius c):
- All charges contribute as if at their respective radii
V_C = (1/4πε₀)(q₁/c + q₂/c + q₃/c) = (1/4πε₀)(q₁ + q₂ + q₃)/c

Therefore the correct answer is option (3).

questions.subject: Physics
questions.text: Identify the correct statements: A. Effective capacitance of a series combination of capacitors is always smaller than the smallest capacitance of the capacitor in the combination. B. When a dielectric medium is placed between the charged plates of a capacitor, displacement of charges cannot occur due to insulation property of dielectric. C. Increasing of area of capacitor plate or decreasing of thickness of dielectric is an alternate method to increase the capacitance. D. For a point charge, concentric spherical shells centered at the location of the charge are equipotential surfaces.
questions.sol_text:
For series combination: 1/C_eq = 1/C_1 + 1/C_2. Therefore C_eq is less than C_1 & C_2. This confirms statement A is correct.

Note: In statement C, capacitor is assumed to be completely filled with dielectric then on decreasing thickness of dielectric capacitance will increase. This confirms statement C is correct.

For a point charge, the electric potential at a distance r is given by V = kQ/r. All points at the same distance from the point charge have the same potential, therefore concentric spherical shells centered at the location of the charge are equipotential surfaces. This confirms statement D is correct.

Statement B is incorrect because when a dielectric medium is placed between the charged plates of a capacitor, polarization occurs (displacement of bound charges in the dielectric), not that it cannot occur.

Therefore, statements A, C and D are correct.

questions.text: A capacitor P with capacitance 10×10^(-6) F is fully charged with a potential difference of 6.0 V and disconnected from the battery. The charged capacitor P is connected across another capacitor Q with capacitance 20×10^(-6) F. The charge on capacitor Q when equilibrium is established will be a×10^(-5) C (assume capacitor Q does not have any charge initially), the value of a is ____.
questions.sol_text:
C_1 = 10^(-5) F
Capacitor P: +| |− V_1 = 6V
Capacitor Q: | |
C_2 = 2×10^(-5) F
V_2 = 0

When equilibrium is established, both capacitors will have the same potential difference.

Using charge conservation:
Total initial charge = Total final charge
C_1 V_1 + C_2 V_2 = (C_1 + C_2)V

where V is the final common voltage

V = (C_1 V_1 + C_2 V_2)/(C_1 + C_2) = (10^(-5) × 6 + 0)/(3×10^(-5))

V = (10^(-5) × 6)/(3×10^(-5)) = 6/3 = 2 volt

Charge on capacitor Q:
Q_2 = C_2 × V = 2×10^(-5) × 2 = 4×10^(-5) C

Therefore, a = 4

questions.subject: Physics
questions.text: The space between the plates of a parallel-plate capacitor of capacitance C (without any dielectric) is now filled with three dielectric slabs of dielectric constants K_1 = 2, K_2 = 3, and K_3 = 5 (as shown in the figure). If new capacitance is (n/3)C then the value of n is ____.
questions.sol_text:
From the figure, the three dielectric slabs are arranged in parallel with the following configuration:
- K_1 = 2 occupies width A/2 and thickness d/2
- K_2 = 3 occupies width A/2 and thickness d/2
- K_3 = 5 occupies width A/2 and thickness d/2

For the slab with K_1 = 2 and dimensions A/2 × d/2:
C_1 = (epsilon_0 K_1 A/2)/(d/2) = (epsilon_0 × 2 × A)/(d) = 5C

For the slab with K_2 = 3 and dimensions A/2 × d/2:
C_2 = (epsilon_0 K_2 A/2)/(d/2) = (epsilon_0 × 2 × 3 × A)/(d) = 2C

C_1 & C_2 are in series:
C' = (C_1 × C_2)/(C_1 + C_2) = ((5C)(2C))/(7C) = (10C)/7

For the slab with K_3 = 5 and dimensions A/2 × d/2:
C_3 = (epsilon_0 K_3 A/2)/(d/2) = (epsilon_0 × 3 × A)/(d) = 3C

For the slab with K_4 = 2 and dimensions A/2 × d/2:
C_4 = (epsilon_0 × 2 × A)/(d) = 2C

C_4 & C_3 are in series:
C'' = ((2C)(3C))/(5C) = (6C)/5

C' & C'' are in parallel:
C_eq = C' + C'' = C((6/5) + (10/7)) = C((42 + 50)/35) = C(92/35)

Since C_eq = (nC)/3:
(92/35)C = (nC)/3
n = (92 × 3)/35 = 276/35 = 7.9 ≈ n = 8
questions.nvt_note: Give your answer as the nearest integer.
